Michael Dukakis Public Service Internship 
The Michael Dukakis Public Service Internship Award provides students with the opportunity to intern in a public 
service or government setting to encourage students to consider a career in public service. This year's interns were: 
Ruiqi Huang ‘29 
Political Science 
Ruiqi Huang, Political Science (Pre- 
Law concentration), is a recipient of the 
Claire T. Carney Leader Internship and 
Chancellor's Scholarship. As a Research 
Assistant, he contributes to research 
on governance and democracy. As an 
intern with MassPIRG's Hunger Free 
Campus Initiative, he worked closely with 
Massachusetts legislators to address 
food insecurity at public universities. 
This summer, Ruiqi interned with the 
Catholic Charities Legal Network in 
Washington, D.C., providing pro bono civil 
legal services and supporting formerly 
incarcerated individuals during reentry. 
Luke Chadwick   ‘27 
Law 
Luke Chadwick is J.D. candidate and Public 
Interest Law Fellow (PILF) at the University 
of Massachusetts School of Law. During 
his time at UMass Law, Luke has worked 
as a Teaching Assistant, Academic Fellow, 
and is a member of the UMass Law Review. 
Luke’s passion for service to others and his 
community is what inspired him to attend 
UMass Law, specifically because of the PILF 
program which makes law school more 
accessible for students seeking to pursue 
careers in public service. This summer, Luke 
was a legal intern with the Massachusetts 
Attorney General’s Office in Boston working 
in the Digital Evidence Lab.
